steps.shell: python3 -I -c "import json,subprocess,os; subprocess.run(['python3','qa/drive.py','--port',os.environ['PORT'],'--display',os.environ['DISPLAY'],'ui','--root','all','--filter','Pixel Preview','--save','/tmp/pp42.json'],capture_output=True,text=True); d=json.load(open('/tmp/pp42.json')); on=[c for c in d['controls'] if c.get('name')=='PixelPreviewButton' and c.get('visible')]; on=bool(on and on[0].get('toggled')); (not on) and subprocess.run(['python3','qa/drive.py','--port',os.environ['PORT'],'--display',os.environ['DISPLAY'],'click-text','Pixel Preview'],capture_output=True,text=True); print('preview on after ensure:', on)"

items.check: Editor viewport with the pixel menu bar on top: Pixel Preview clicked OFF reveals the raw smooth scene with the editor grid and coloured origin axes, then clicked ON again restores the pixel look and hides the grid. Poster shows the pixel look ON with the cursor on Pixel Preview (no stray tooltip).
items.notes: The scene's renderer has studio_prelook on, but the 3D-view Pixel Preview button state at session start is not guaranteed; a shell step reads the button's toggled state and clicks it once if needed so the clip always starts ON. Then the two recorded clicks go OFF then ON.

items.check: The Pixel World panel's lower section (Lighting Preset buttons + Wire Sun / Env Refs button + the hint line) with a sliver of the NORMAL DAYTIME pixel viewport on the left (no dusk/orange), the cursor hovering Wire Sun / Env Refs showing its tooltip, then clicking it.
items.notes: Window is 1040 tall so the Pixel World panel fits; the panel is scrolled down 10 wheel steps to bring the Wire Sun / Env Refs button to ~y617. Crop is the panel + left viewport sliver, which keeps the daytime look (the old shot had a leftover Dusk-preset orange sky). The click at 1178,617 is verified present by the preceding ui expect.

items.check: Same close crop of the ruin's tower/roof edge against the sky: with Outline Off there is no dark edge; with Outline On a clear dark outline traces the silhouette (2x nearest upscale).
items.notes: Pixel Preview is ON by default. Focus the ruin mesh first (select the Ruin child, middle-click the view, F) because the default editor camera is 45 m away; then select BuilderRuin, move the mouse over the view and press Esc (clears the yellow builder selection box), and frame the wall from ~20 m. Outline 0/1 is set by path; crop 600,330,300,150 around the tower/roof edge against the sky, upscaled 2x with NEAREST. Camera unchanged between the two shots.
